newsitem.title: CHILE: Latam stocks seen drifting in hesitant mood.
newsitem.headline: Latam stocks seen drifting in hesitant mood.

text.p: Most Latin American markets are seen drifting sideways this week with investors looking to domestic issues and to Wall Street's opening after the Labor Day break Monday, said traders.

The independent-minded Caracas bourse is likely to be the most buoyant with blue chips expected to swing higher following the government's announcement Friday that it would go ahead with Banco de Venezuela sale, said traders.
"The government's still making good noises about privatization. This week the bolsa could well rise on foreign bids after the U.S. long weekend," said Capital Markets broker Ricardo Marino.
Last week's surprise suspension of the bank's sale had dented market sentiment and sent stocks spinning.
The Caracas bolsa' 19-share index ended the week flat at 4,601.31 points after early gains were wiped out by the suspended auction.

Argentine blue chip shares, which closed higher last week, are expected to float range-bound in nervous trade with eyes on a possible Congressional debate midweek on controversial tax measures, said brokers.
The selective Merval index recouped some recent losses last week to close up 1.8 percent at 509.43 points. It shed 3.8 percent in August.
"The Merval is hovering between 490-510 points but it's not clear which way it's going," said Luis Enrique Alvarez of brokerage Alvarez.
Congress could start screening Wednesday tax reforms unveiled by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez but analysts fear the discussion may be delayed by another week.

Mexican stocks are expected to hold steady as analysts revise their growth estimates as the result of economic figures given by President Ernesto Zedillo during his second state of the nation address Sunday, said brokers.

"In our basic scenario the presidential report will be positive for the markets and negative factors which may appear connected with it will not be significant," said a report from brokers BBV-Probursa.
Mexican blue chips closed last week down 1.75 percent at 3,305.47 points.
In Brazil, investors can expect stocks to firm later in the week on bargain-hunting after a slow start, said traders.

"The market's recent weakness can ecourage investors to rebuild positions," said one senior trader, referring to benchmark Telebras which fell to a 75 real level after climbing to over 77 reais on expectations of a new telephone rate hike later this year.
But the bolsa could be undercut if Wall Street continues to slide on lower bond prices, said traders.
The selective Bovespa index ended last week up a scant 0.91 percent at 62,594 points.
Fears over possible rises in U.S. interest rates are also seen unsettling Chilean blue chips this week, said traders.
"If U.S. rates increase, this will aggravate the apathy which has taken hold of the market," said one trader.
Santiago's bolsa is seen continuing weak in light volume with high local interest rates making fixed income investments much more attractive than stocks, said traders.
The 40-share IPSA index ended last week down 1.62 percent at 96.06 points.
